headlines.article_text: Anthropic IPO live updates: ANT stock price and Nasdaq debut Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 1:10 01:10 Anthropic opens at $111.50 per share in record IPO Squawk on the Street Anthropic opened at $111.50 per share in the artificial intelligence lab's Nasdaq debut on Thursday after the company completed the biggest initial public offering on record. The stock will trade under the ticker "ANT" after the company raised $81.3 billion in the IPO. The Claude creator sold 980 million shares at $83 a piece on Wednesday, lifting the size and price of its offering. The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. Highlights so far: Market cap tops $2 trillion in debut, putting it among the tech titans ANT stock pops in first trade Protesters gather outside the Nasdaq Daniela Amodei gives a shoutout to mom Dario Amodei addresses debt and landing an investment-grade credit rating Spotted: Executives sporting "Clawd" pins at Nasdaq Dario Amodei renews pledge to pace frontier AI development Retail demand for ANT was the largest in history Anthropic employees set to get rich CNBC's reporters are covering Anthropic's IPO live on air and online from our bureaus in San Francisco and Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, and from the Nasdaq in New York City. VIDEO 15:11 15:11 Watch CNBC’s full interview with Anthropic co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei 4 Min Ago Menlo Ventures has $25 billion aggregate position in Anthropic, partner Matt Murphy says Menlo Ventures partner Matt Murphy, an early Anthropic investor, said the firm's aggregate position in the AI company is around $25 billion. "Clearly the most epic return for Menlo Ventures in our history, and one of the top handful in the history of venture capital," Murphy told CNBC in an interview. "We feel grateful. We have over five LPs that we've delivered over a billion dollars of returns to, and at the end of the day, you know that that that's really our job." — Ashley Capoot 10 Min Ago Ashton Kutcher celebrates Anthropic IPO Michael Kovac Ashton Kutcher congratulated Dario Amodei and "the whole team at Anthropic" in a post on X shortly before the AI company's first trade. Kutcher co-founded Sound Ventures , a Los Angeles-based venture capital firm, which invested in Anthropic in 2023 and participated in several subsequent funding rounds. The VC firm also counts Guy Oseary, the legendary talent manager for musicians including Madonna, among its cofounders. Bloomberg reported that Sound Ventures owns roughly half a percent of Anthropic, citing sources familiar with the matter. Sound Ventures' stake is likely now worth billions of dollars after the company's lofty IPO. — Annie Palmer 15 Min Ago Bessemer's Deeter calls Anthropic IPO a "Google moment" Byron Deeter, a partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, called Anthropic 's IPO a " Google moment" for the frontier lab during CNBC's Halftime Report. At over $2 trillion in market capitalization, Anthropic has entered Google's ranks as one of the most valuable companies in the world, behind Apple , Microsoft , Nvidia , Alphabet (Google's parent company), and Amazon . But Deeter says Anthropic doesn't need to "dominate intelligence" in the same way that Google dominates search. The artificial intelligence ecosystem will see "multiple great businesses," Deeter says, adding that he expects Anthropic to continue to be a market leader while also pacing the frontier of AI model development. — Isabel O'Brien 19 Min Ago Anthropic’s governance structure Anthropic Co-Founder and CEO Dario Amodei speaks at Dreamforce 2026 summit in San Francisco, California, U.S., September 15, 2026. Carlos Barria | Reuters Anthropic has an unusual governance structure . The company is a public benefit corporation, which means it's required to balance the financial interest of stockholders, the best interests of those affected by its conduct and its "company purpose." Anthropic said in its prospectus that its purpose is to facilitate the "responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity." Anthropic's seven co-founders also wield a lot of power over the company. Prior to the completion of its offering, Anthropic issued a single share of Class F common stock to a limited liability company called "Founder LLC." Anthropic's co-founders are the sole members of Founder LLC, and the entity holds 50.1% of the voting power of the company's outstanding shares. Each co-founder sold 3.38 million shares in the IPO, according to the prospectus, for total proceeds of $1.96 billion. Additionally, Anthropic introduced an independent governance body called the " Long-Term Benefit Trust " in 2023, which has the authority to elect and remove the majority of the company's board of directors. — Ashley Capoot 31 Min Ago Anthropic's market cap tops $2 trillion in Nasdaq debut Anthropic opened with a market capitalization of nearly $2.01 trillion, behind only Apple , Microsoft , Nvidia , Alphabet and Amazon . — Ashley Capoot 49 Min Ago Ben Bernanke is in the room Ben Bernanke T.J. Kirkpatrick | Bloomberg | Getty Images Ben Bernanke, the former chair of the Federal Reserve , is in the room at the Nasdaq as investors celebrate Anthropic's first trade. Anthropic in July appointed Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, the AI company's independent governance structure that advises it and appoints its board members. — Annie Palmer 50 Min Ago Anthropic shares pop 34% in Nasdaq debut Anthropic shares popped 34% in the company's Nasdaq debut. Anthropic requires every employee to pass a culture interview, which is taken very seriously, Amodei said. He added that he spends roughly half of his time focusing on talent and culture at the company. "We've been very disciplined about turning down people who are deeply technically talented, but who don't fit our culture," Amodei said. "We don't want people who are jerks. The company is buying AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion to secure open-weight models. In this article PANW Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT VIDEO 10:50 10:50 You need to train AI and security at the same time, says Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora Palo Alto Networks shares rose 6% on Thursday as businesses boosted spending on cybersecurity products and investors cheered the company's acquisition of a startup that pushes it into securing open-weight artificial intelligence models. The company beat Wall Street's estimates for the fiscal first quarter. Revenue jumped 39% from a year ago and Palo Alto boosted its guidance for the year. Recent outages at Microsoft , banks and the Federal Aviation Administration have left businesses reeling. While U.S. officials haven't detected any malicious activity, the disruptions raise concerns over aging equipment and infrastructure. Many businesses are scrambling to patch vulnerabilities at a faster clip than ever before to keep pace with the growing risks of AI-powered cyberattacks. Those fears have led more businesses to consolidate platforms, which is fueling growth in areas like firewall and AI security, Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora told CNBC's " Mad Money " on Wednesday. "They're going to have to make sure they get the best players in the market to come support them because this is no longer child's play," Arora said. It's one of several recent deals in Arora's aggressive acquisition spree and marks a significant shift beyond cybersecurity. "Rather than being one player out of 10 in the industry serving compute, we want to be the one player with Palo Alto that delivers secure compute and security capability," Arora told CNBC. Palo Alto expects the deal to add more than $1 billion in annual recurring revenue to its next-generation security business by the 2029 fiscal year. Analysts at Bank of America touted the deal as a "bold move" to expand beyond securing AI into training open-weight models, allowing Palo Alto to lead the next phase of the AI revolution. This "appears consistent with PANW's 'long-game' - become indispensable beyond cyber into multidisciplinary IT domains across AI-value-chain," wrote analysts at Citigroup. A banner on its homepage states the bill, dubbed the Delivery Protection Act, "could add up to $5 per order." Amazon has lobbied heavily against the proposed legislation, while New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani backed the bill earlier this year. In this article AMZN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT An Amazon driver loads packages into a delivery van at an Amazon delivery station in Alpharetta, Georgia, Nov. 28, 2022. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images Amazon is taking its fight against a New York City delivery bill, which has been backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani , to its shopping website and app. Some users who open the company's shopping app or website report being served with pop-ups and banners warning that the New York City Council "could add up to $5 per order" if it passes Intro 518, or the Delivery Protection Act. The bill would require Amazon to employ its army of third-party delivery companies directly, disrupting the contractor model it has relied on since 2018. Amazon uses a network of thousands of small companies, who often solely work for Amazon, to handle the last-mile portion of shipments, in an effort to speed up deliveries and control more of its logistics operations. "If this legislation passes, we'd no longer be able to work with them, and we'd be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city," Amazon's in-app message states. "That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees." The proposed legislation was introduced in February and is awaiting review by City Council Speaker Julie Menin. Amazon also posted a statement on its company website where it often publishes its policy positions . But rarely has it used its valuable e-commerce site and app real estate to push its perspectives. Other tech companies including Uber and Lyft have similarly used their apps to advocate for or against legislation in the past. Amazon's pop-up notices and a stationary banner on its store homepage direct users to a form where they can "contact your council member to oppose Intro 518." The Delivery Protection Act has received a swell of support from labor groups, including the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, which has sought to unionize Amazon delivery and warehouse workers. Mamdani endorsed the bill in August, saying Amazon's subcontractor model "leaves workers vulnerable and corporations free to avoid accountability for reckless conditions on city streets." He's argued the bill would lead to safer working conditions for drivers, and allow the city to "regulate last-mile operations." Amazon has lobbied heavily against the bill, while business groups have launched local advertising campaigns, and warned they may sue the city if the bill passes.
